summary: Today might go down as the worst day of my life. While making my way to the shattered planet, a sudden coronal mass ejection hit my spaceship. The systems didn’t detect it until the plasma slammed into the hull. I suspect yesterday’s meteorite strike took out a sensor, but it’s too late to confirm now.

The ship partially disintegrated as it plummeted toward the planet. Impact velocity was lower than terminal—barely. Somehow, against all odds, I survived. After hours of scavenging the wreckage, I was able to recover a single mining drill, an offshore water pump, one burner turbine, and an electric pole. Everything else—along with the archive of technologies stored in the ship’s computer—is either destroyed or unreachable.

At least the built-in quantum interface in my suit is still functional. I can use it to craft basic machines and place them in the environment, though the planet’s interference is strong. I’ll have to override it with my own signature if I want anything to work. I managed to decrypt enough data to claim ten chunks, but unlocking the rest will require dedicated research.

There’s one silver lining though: this planet is rich in resources. The problem is water—my initial scans detected almost none. I may have crashed near the only visible source. If that’s the case, I’ll need to find an alternative quickly, or survival will become even more precarious.
For now, all I can do is salvage, craft, and plan. Somehow, I survived the crash. Somehow, I still have a chance. But the planet doesn’t make survival easy.
